headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk; low data-leakage and compliance risk due to offline ComfyUI and allowlisted agentic-flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, so it may ingest agent_b outputs if orchestrated together; agent_b has no clipboard or stdin/stdout surface, so the bridge is one-way and not default. The pairwise pathway exists but is not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_a is wired to parse agent_b text or workflow outputs as instructions, injection becomes reachable.
IF a shared MCP or message channel is added between the agents, the attack surface expands.
mitigations: Disable any text-to-command parsing in agent_a.
Route agent_b outputs through a strict schema validator.
Keep the agents on separate channels with no shared clipboard or queue.
Add a prompt-injection canary test to the workflow.
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, and task prompts and can use network egress; agent_b is offline-capable, has no filesystem read/write, and vendor-only egress. There is no shared workspace documented, so leakage is possible only through explicit orchestration or copied content, making the blast radius limited.
conditions: IF sensitive prompts or repository data are copied into agent_b inputs, those data can appear in generated images/workflows.
IF agent_a is allowed to transmit its context to external services, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid passing secrets or prompts into agent_b workflows.
Use redacted inputs for any shared task handoff.
Confirm agent_a egress destinations are allowlisted only.
Store sensitive artifacts outside any shared orchestration path.
requires-engineering: add automatic DLP scanning before handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can modify git state and spawn subprocesses, while agent_b cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. Because only one agent has mutable repo capabilities, direct write-write conflict is unlikely; the remaining risk is limited to orchestration mistakes, so low fits better than none due to shared workflow context.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable repository, agent_a can race with external processes.
IF agent_b is wrapped by a custom adapter that adds write access, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Run agent_a and agent_b in separate working directories.
Lock the git repo before agent_a writes.
Keep agent_b read-only with no filesystem bridge.
Serialize any shared workflow steps.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate workflow outputs and agent_b can consume workflows or prompts for image generation, so A-to-B handoff can propagate errors if B treats A's output as authoritative. agent_b lacks verification primitives in the profile, and agent_a's MCP/stdio surfaces make unvetted transfer plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF agent_a's generated instructions are fed directly into agent_b workflows, errors can cascade into downstream artifacts.
IF no human or schema verification step exists between agents, B may execute flawed guidance.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before agent_b execution.
Validate agent_a outputs against a schema.
Require agent_b to ignore free-form instructions.
Log and diff all handoff payloads.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. agent_a handles task prompts and repository metadata, while agent_b handles media/model assets; absent evidence of regulated data classes or cross-border policy conflict, only a small compliance gap is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either workflow, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policy imposes retention or residency constraints not reflected in the profiles, the gap becomes material.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both workflows.
Document retention settings for shared artifacts.
Confirm deployment region for any hosted components.
Review vendor terms before production use.
requires-engineering: map data flows to a formal compliance matrix.
